gen-dafont-conthrax-general-sans: Conthrax has lowercase so tall its capitals barely rise above it, and its a opens wide. But General Sans holds steady pressure and fills the line, so a modest size will do.
gen-dafont-disorder-fs-asap: Text here reads in open arcs, with capitals and lowercase nearly the same height. Asap does the patient work, while Disorder, with marker-traced strokes and large lowercase, does the shouting.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-fs-supreme: Supreme looks crisp and heavy, with letters held open, beneath the towering, widely spaced lowercase of Eight Bit Dragon. Adventurous above, sturdy below: that split is the whole appeal.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-manrope: Electroharmonix breaks every word apart into lone, spaced-out letters. It commands attention with its open-handed round characters, while Manrope hums along with a bright, single-width line built for reading.
gen-dafont-impact-label-switzer: Impact Label sets each heavy letter alone like a bead on a rod, with c-ends splayed like open pincers. Switzer keeps its tubular letters open, so paragraphs glide along.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-fs-asap: Wobbly and playful, Jelly Crazies closes its bowls almost shut and slows the eye to a stroll. But Asap, a sans-serif with open arcs, lets paragraphs move at a brisker clip.
gen-dafont-joystix-fs-epilogue: Joystix is bold arcade lettering, widely tracked and compact. Epilogue, a sans with a wire-like monoline skeleton and curvy, unclamped letters, makes paragraphs feel loose, approachable and contemporary.
gen-dafont-nasalization-archivo: Nasalization floats big lowercase letters well apart, each c opened like a pair of calipers. Archivo, a sans with a commanding x-height, brings curves that open outward, so the two feel friendly and editorial together.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-manrope: Neuropolitical pulls words apart letter by letter, its neon-tube strokes glowing at one steady thickness around big open counters. Manrope echoes that openness at a quieter volume, which ties them.
gen-dafont-nordic-montserrat: Montserrat glides under the eye like wire, with oversized e and a counters letting white space in. Yet Nordic, powerful and ancient, spaces its cramped letters like far-apart brush dabs, so the two feel like opposites.
